limitations_and_boundaries: The method is designed for additive nonlinear models with arbitrary noise, but its performance may degrade under model misspecification.
The experimental evaluation is limited to synthetic data and one real-world dataset (Sachs).
The algorithm assumes the causal graph is a DAG and that the SCM is identifiable under the additive noise model.

research_questions.statement: Can we develop a causal discovery method for additive nonlinear models with arbitrary noise distributions?

provenance.text_excerpt: This leads to NoGAM (Not only Gaussian Additive noise Models), a causal discovery algorithm with a minimal set of assumptions and state of the art performance, experimentally benchmarked on synthetic data.

claims.statement: NoGAM is a causal discovery algorithm with a minimal set of assumptions and state-of-the-art performance.

experiments_or_tasks: Design of NoGAM, a causal discovery algorithm for additive nonlinear models with generic noise distributions, using score matching to infer topological ordering.

methods.name: NoGAM
methods.protocol_description: NoGAM infers the topological ordering of variables in a causal graph from data generated by an additive nonlinear model with arbitrary noise. It uses a relation between the score function (gradient of log-likelihood) and residual estimators to iteratively identify leaf nodes. The algorithm then prunes the graph using the CAM pruning method.
